findings.message: Round 1 asked for every tool_result to be redacted, quoted and checked for injection. The error path now quotes the message and checks it for injection, but it never redacts it. The success path is redacted ('tool results and nested data are redacted and quoted'), and the stated reason for this fix is that errors 'can echo record values'. Quoting a value doesn't hide it, so classified data in a DB or tool error still reaches the provider. Fix: run the error text through the same redaction as results. Better still, send a fixed string ('read_ticket failed', plus a logError reference) and keep the raw message server-side. Add a test where the error message contains a classified value or an email address.
findings.scenario: Tool run throws a Postgres unique-violation `Key (email)=(kasun@lumen.test) already exists` or a check error that includes a pay figure → the provider receives `<data label="error from create_person">…kasun@lumen.test…</data>` unredacted, even with redaction enabled for the tenant.

findings.message: The fix for reordered environments only works when the projects' orders don't contradict each other. When they do (a cycle), stageColumns falls back to position/name order, and ReleaseMap still assumes 'columns agree with it'. lastI = max column index of reached stages, so the line is drawn past columns the project hasn't reached, while `back` is read from the last stage in the project's own order. The round-1 finding offered drawing each row by its own s.position as the alternative, and that handles this case. The only contradiction test checks that each name appears once, not what gets drawn. Fix: in ReleaseMap, place each row's stations and line by its own stage order (or flag rows whose order disagrees with the columns). Add a test with two projects that order the same environments in opposite ways and check the drawn extent.
findings.scenario: Project X: Dev, UAT, Staging, Prod. Project Y: Dev, Staging, UAT, Prod. The cycle fallback gives columns Dev, Staging, UAT, Prod (ties by name) or similar. Y has reached Dev and Staging, and UAT is the furthest it reached in its own order → lastI points at the UAT column, so for X the line is drawn through Staging as if it had been reached. For Y, in the other column order, the line covers UAT, which it hasn't reached.

findings.message: This adds a project row lock to syncProposal and claims it makes sync and createProposal safe together ('keys share one namespace'). No test runs a syncProposal and a createProposal at the same time on one project. The existing race test only runs concurrent createProposal calls, so it stays green if this new lock is deleted. Fix: add a race test with two real sessions, one syncing a specclaw key and one creating a proposal in the same project, and assert the keys are distinct and nothing is lost.
findings.scenario: Delete the new `select 1 ... for update` line → every test in the diff still passes.

findings.message: The test 're-running with nothing changed writes and audits nothing' used to count all audit rows. It now counts only `delivery.proposal.sync` rows, so an unchanged re-sync that writes other audits (project update, phase_changed, withdraw) would still pass. The diff doesn't explain why it was narrowed. Either restore the count of all audits or explain the excluded action.
findings.scenario: A re-sync that writes a `delivery.project.update` audit on every run → the test stays green.

findings.message: When the server commits a confirm but the response is lost, the catch block brings the buttons back with 'Try again'. A retry then gets 'no longer pending', and the card shows it as `cancelled`, even though the write happened. Map the 'no longer pending' reply to a neutral 'already handled' state rather than 'cancelled'.
findings.scenario: confirmChat commits and the network drops before the response → the user clicks 'Add it' again → the card says cancelled, but the proposal exists.

findings.message: The migration hard-codes a second copy of the REGIONS code/name table from packages/ai/src/policy.ts. It is a one-off, so the risk is limited, but add a comment saying it is a snapshot that must match REGIONS as of this migration.

The proposal retention clock starts only at `delivery.proposal.released`. A proposal that is never released keeps `owner_name` with no end date: one withdrawn by sync, one cancelled, or one still open on an abandoned project. The project entry has the same gap: the clock starts at `delivery.project.closed`, so a project that is abandoned and never formally closed keeps `manager_name` forever. The fix covers the happy path, not every way a record can end. Fix: start the clock at the record's terminal state, whichever comes first (released or withdrawn, closed or archived), or add a fallback start such as last update. Also check at manifest load that every `start` names an event the module actually emits (`start` is a free string today).
findings.scenario: Sync withdraws AMX-042 (its folder is deleted on main) → no delivery.proposal.released event is ever emitted → the 032 retention job never anonymises the owner_name on AMX-042

findings.message: take() changed behaviour in a second way that no test covers. Before, when main's state.json was unreadable, a readable overlay replaced the record. Now `if (cur?.unreadable) return;` keeps it unreadable and reports the main source. The tests only cover 'main unreadable, no overlay' and 'overlay unreadable'. Add the 'main unreadable + readable overlay' row so that decision is pinned.
findings.scenario: main 001-a state.json corrupt, branch specclaw/001-a readable at Implementing → the record is skipped (reported at main@…); no test fixes which result is intended

findings.message: The variant test covers ForbiddenError, a generic Error and a working module, but not ScopeError, which is the second class the fix now checks with instanceof. Add a ScopeError row so a wrong import (a second ScopeError copy, or the wrong package) fails the test.
findings.scenario: ScopeError imported from a different module instance than the one search functions throw → a scoped-out module is reported in notSearched; no test catches it
